topic: AI basics: what a "model" is, and why Claude has Haiku, Sonnet, Opus and Fable
post:
Haiku, Sonnet, Opus, Fable… why does Claude have so many names? 🤔
Here's what a "model" is, in plain English.

A model is the AI "brain" behind the chat window. It's what actually reads your message and writes the answer.

Claude isn't one model. It's a family, like a team of specialists.

Here's how Anthropic describes today's lineup:

⚡ Haiku: the fastest, built for high-volume, simple tasks
⚖️ Sonnet: "the best combination of speed and intelligence"
🧠 Opus: for long-running coding and knowledge work
🏔️ Fable: for the most demanding reasoning and long, multi-step work

The trade-off is simple: more powerful models are usually slower, faster ones are lighter.

How to switch:
In the Claude app, click the model name next to the send button and pick another one. (Which models you see depends on your plan.)

A simple rule to start:
Quick rewrite or summary? Try a faster model.
Big, tricky task with lots of steps? Try a more powerful one.

Why it matters:
Picking the right model is like picking the right tool. You don't need a sledgehammer to hang a picture. 🔨

Which model do you use most? 👇

Follow me: I'm teaching one Claude skill a day, no tech background needed.
